Together with the previous inequalities this establishes every spacing condition used in the flat convergence argument. A nearest-neighbor coordinate path from x to z has length a = |z −x|1 and stays within that distance of x. Such a path is obtained by changing each integer coordinate toward its target one unit at a time. The Atlas one-step data supply a weighted forward directional difference row bounded by c/Ld+1.
